title: API key lifecycle: rotation, expiry, naming, and per-scope tokens
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Design and implement a hardened API token model for Redwood Admin Controls that supports per-scope tokens, automated rotation & expiry, standard naming conventions, and full audit-log visibility. This ticket covers: 1) API surface changes (backend + Console) for per-scope keys; 2) token lifecycle policies (rotation enforcement, max lifetime, grace periods); 3) migration path for existing v1 tokens to the new governance model; 4) integration with audit logging & SSO identity correlation; 5) alerting + telemetry for compromised or out-of-policy tokens.

Motivation: Current token model is simple bearer tokens without fine-grained scopes or enforced rotation. For enterprise customers and Private deployments we need: scoped credentials (least privilege), enforceable rotation/expiry to reduce blast radius, human-friendly naming for admin ops, and clear audit trails tied to SSO identities and RBAC-v2 roles. This is a prerequisite for completing RBAC v2 and meeting enterprise compliance requests.
acceptance_criteria: Backend: token metadata supports scopes (list), name, creator_identity, created_at, expires_at, last_rotated_at, rotation_enforced boolean.
Console: token creation UI allows selecting scopes, naming token, setting optional expiry, and shows rotation state. Tokens created in Console are displayed only once (value shown at creation).
Rotation: system-level policy can be configured (default 90 days) and optionally enforced per-organization. Enforcement must block long-lived tokens and emit audit events for non-compliant tokens.
Per-scope enforcement: runtime rejects requests where token scope does not cover the attempted operation and logs audit event with reason code.

Audit logs: every token create/rotate/expire/revoke/usage event is logged with SSO identity if available and route info; logs surface in Console Activity feed and external SIEM via existing forwarding pipeline.
Migration: existing tokens are importable into v2 model with an opt-in grace window and automated notifications for owners to rotate or assign scopes.
Security review: design and implementation pass security review and threat model sign-off documented in Confluence.
Load: token lookup and scope-check path adds <5% latency overhead p50 in auth-critical path (benchmarked).
tasks: Design API schema changes: add token model fields and scope enum (auth service).
Instrumentation: audit event schemas and log forwarding mapping for new token events.
Console mockups: token creation flow, name validation, rotation UI, token listing with filters.
Backend implementation: storage migration, scope enforcement in gateway, rotation worker.
Migration tooling: script to import v1 tokens with owner lookup and notification emails.
E2E tests: unit + integration tests for scope enforcement, rotation worker, and audit events.
Performance testing: benchmark auth path with token lookup cache warmed vs cold.
Run security review and incorporate feedback.
Prepare rollout plan and runbook for incidents.
Create customer-facing docs and admin guides (Drive/Confluence).
comments: 2025-02-19 - Aisha Kumar: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/API+Key+Lifecycle. Agreed initial default max lifetime = 90 days, optional org override allowed.

2025-02-24 - Liam O'Connor: POC for scope enforcement completed. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123 (WIP). Observed ~2.8% p50 auth latency increase without caching; will add local token cache in gateway.

2025-02-27 - Security Review (preliminary): Suggested adding cryptographic key-id rotation support for long-lived integrator tokens and revocation list check in gateway. See review notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SecReviewNotes.

2025-03-01 - Product (Maya Chen): UX feedback - require token name pattern to include purpose and environment (eg. 'svc-reporting-prod'). Product requests per-scope presets for common roles (read-only embeddings, generate-only).
2025-03-03 - Eng (Carlos Rivera): Implemented audit event schema v2 and wired logs to SIEM staging. Verified token_create and token_rotate events include sso_subject and session_id where available.
2025-03-05 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented migration script draft and email template for notify->rotate flow. Putting migration behind feature flag and will schedule canary to 5% orgs.
2025-03-05 - QA (Priya Desai): Added integration test plan; will validate console display behavior and that token values are not retrievable after creation.
migration_plan: Phase 0 (Design): bake model & policy with Security and PM signoff.
Phase 1 (Canary): deploy backend-only changes and migration script behind feature flag; enable read-only views for v2 tokens for 5% orgs.
Phase 2 (Notify): run migration script in dry-run mode, send notifications to token owners for 50% orgs, collect feedback and fix UX issues.
Phase 3 (Enforce): enable rotation enforcement and scope-required checks for new tokens; existing tokens get grace window of 60 days to rotate.
Phase 4 (Complete): after grace window and audits, expire any non-rotated tokens and require re-creation with scopes; full rollout and update customer docs.
ui_notes: Token creation modal: name (required), description (optional), scopes (multi-select with search), expiry (optional, default org-policy), enforce rotation (checkbox visible to org-admins).
Token list: searchable by name, creator, scope, created_at, last_rotated_at; show warning badge for tokens approaching expiry or out-of-policy.
Rotation workflow: 'Rotate' action generates new value shown once, marks old token rotated and keeps old token valid for configurable grace (default 24h).
Activity feed: token events are filterable (create/rotate/revoke/usage) and link to related session or SSO identity when available.
RBAC notes: only org-admins + role with token_manage permission can create or revoke org-level tokens; service accounts can create scoped tokens limited to their project.
open_questions: Default max lifetime: 90 days recommended. Do we need shorter default for Hosted vs Private?
Rotation enforcement for CI/CD pipelines: allow emergency 'service token' exemption with stricter audit and HSM-backed storage?
Should we support asymmetric key-based tokens (kid + signature) in v1 of this project or defer to later phase?
Exact mapping of scope enums to runtime capability bits needs review with runtime team to avoid frequent schema churn.
